meta.task: P2 (target material parameters: what values, what source, was a citation given) + P7 (validity floor for the high-frequency approximation: minimum electrical size, facet-per-wavelength rule, kr threshold) answered from the SIONNA corpus, with the drone/RCS-anchor corpus used only as labelled secondary context.
meta.axis: OUR problems are the columns. For each paper: did it MEET the problem on its own claim path, and if so what did it do - solve / work around / ignore / never met it.
meta.evidence_rule: Every paper-level claim below carries pdf_path + page + a verbatim quote from the PDF text layer. Anything produced by regex over PDF text is labelled evidence_type=machine_count. Anything not opened page by page says NOT_OPENED.

secondary_drone_rcs.use: structural / negative-space context only, plus two RCS_ANCHOR papers opened for P7 because P7 explicitly asks for every validity rule with its source

meta.tooling: PyMuPDF (fitz) text layer, full document; text cached per PDF under the session scratchpad
known_limits: 14 of 140 Sionna papers were opened page by page in this task. The other 126 contribute ONLY machine counts and are never described as having or lacking a property beyond what the regex literally shows.

The regex-derived numbers are corpus-level marker counts, not semantic judgements. A marker can be a false positive (verified example: 'multi-faceted' in 2506.20248 fires the /facet/ pattern; 'low-altitude' fires a case-insensitive /itu/ pattern - this second one was caught and discarded during this task before it became a claim).
Absence of a word is evidence about the paper's TEXT, not proof the authors never thought about it. Rows say which.
self_correction_log: During this task a case-insensitive /itu/ scan on the LAMBDA PDF returned 54 hits. Inspection showed the hits were substrings of 'low-altitude' and similar. The word-boundary count is 12 and all 12 are ITU-R M.2160 / P.838-3 / P.840-9 references, i.e. atmosphere and IMT vision, NOT ITU-R P.2040 materials. P.2040 count in LAMBDA is 0. The 54 was discarded and never used.

headline_findings.claim: NOBODY in the Sionna corpus sourced a TARGET material parameter from a measurement. Zero papers. Our P2 gap is the field's gap.
headline_findings.support: 6 papers state something about a target's electromagnetic properties (rows P2-01..P2-06). Every one of them is either a stock/idealised class (Wood, PEC, 'metallic'), a modelling constant with no source (scattering coefficient 1), or silence. The only measurement-sourced material values anywhere in the corpus are for BUILDING surfaces (rows P2-07..P2-09).

headline_findings.claim: The one author who went deepest on target scattering in Sionna states outright that realistic material properties are FUTURE WORK.
headline_findings.quote: the incorporation of realistic material properties is left for future work

headline_findings.claim: md-rt's 'Wood' propeller is NOT justified anywhere. The word 'Wood' occurs exactly once in the whole 6-page paper - as a table cell. The accompanying sentence defers to Sionna defaults.
quotes: The model's coordinates are located at its geometric center, and electromagnetic parameters such as conductivity are based on Sionna's built-in settings.
headline_findings.machine_count: wood=1, conductivity=1, permittivity=0, facet=0, wavelength-symbol=0 over 6 pages (all 6 pages read)
headline_findings.was_it_on_their_path: MOSTLY NO. Their claims are micro-Doppler RIDGE POSITIONS, which follow from kinematics and are material-independent. BUT their Section IV-B does make an amplitude claim across carrier frequency ('the echo energy of high-frequency signals significantly decreases'), and they attribute it to path loss and, hedged, to atmospheric absorption - never to the target's frequency-dependent scattering. So the one place material WAS on their path, they routed around it.

headline_findings.claim: Clutter-Aware ISAC never states any target material at all. Not 'stock Fresnel' - nothing. The words permittivity, conductivity, dielectric and Fresnel each occur 0 times in both versions. What it claims is a capability, not a value.
headline_findings.quote: The ToI and UAVs are modeled as simplified 3-D mesh objects imported into Sionna. These meshes are obtained by simplifying publicly available 3-D models in Blender and exporting them in Sionna's XML format, which keeps the ray-tracing scene lightweight while enabling flexible material assignment.
headline_findings.correction_to_our_own_prior_note: Our earlier note said Clutter-Aware 'accepts stock Fresnel'. That is OUR inference. The paper never writes the word Fresnel. The defensible statement is: the target material is never reported.

headline_findings.claim: P7: exactly ONE paper in the Sionna corpus gives a quantitative validity floor for its high-frequency approximation, and it is a FACET rule, not a kr rule.
quotes: In addition to the curvature-related metric, the facet size should be of several wavelengths in order to satisfy the UTD assumptions, typically E > 1.5 lambda.

when a single mesh simultaneously has to be used for both backscattering and shadow region prediction, the interval E^2/(R*lambda) ~= 0.6-0.9 provides a practical compromise between accuracy in both regions and computational complexity

headline_findings.claim: The SAME author, in the published conference version, says the facet floor is UNRESOLVED. This is the field admitting it has no defensible discretisation rule.
quotes: The question of how finely curved surface regions need to be discretized in ray-based modeling to achieve results that match ground-truth data for smooth surfaces, remains unresolved and requires further investigation.
even when dealing with electrically small facets and edges; however, how small the facets should be is still an open question

headline_findings.claim: ADVERSARIAL, AGAINST US. An independent published SBR+PO solver validated against analytical Mie puts the optical-region boundary at kr ~ 30. Our airframes span kr 8.4-80 and our own ladder claims 1 dB from kr >= 9.06. Their tolerance is ~2.5% std dev, ours is 1 dB. The two are not contradictory but our claim window is roughly 3.6x more aggressive in kr than the published one, and our worst case (mini5pro at LTE, kr 8.4) sits below BOTH floors.
quotes: Electrical size is here defined as kr = 2*pi*r/lambda, where r is the sphere radius. At kr = 1, Mie resonances dominate and ray tracing methods fail, as wave effects cannot be neglected in this regime. Ray-based approximations become valid as frequency increases, with good agreement typically expected for kr >~ 30. Our simulation results (Fig. 4) demonstrate excellent agreement with Mie theory beginning at an electrical size around kr ~= 30.

the optical region where the method accurately approximates scattering with a standard deviation of ~2.5%. ... The labels kr = 30 and kr = 8000 denote the boundary of the optical region and the onset of the aliasing instability, respectively.
headline_findings.corpus: secondary (RCS_ANCHOR F11) - it is a SBR+PO solver paper, not a Sionna paper
headline_findings.action_for_us: Our P7 statement must cite this number and state explicitly that mini5pro-at-LTE is outside it, rather than resting on our own sphere ladder alone.

headline_findings.claim: QUANTIFIED COST OF UNSOURCED MATERIALS. Using uncalibrated ITU-R P.2040 values in a Sionna scene costs 4.93 dB mean absolute log error in channel gain; gradient calibration against measured CSI brings it to 2.16 dB, and a neural per-point material field to 1.00 dB. This is the closest thing the corpus has to a price tag on our own P2 gap - and it is for WALLS, where the values are at least tabulated. Our target gamma_po has no table at all.
headline_findings.quote: TABLE II: Error statistics | Metric ALE (power) RAE (delay spread) | ITU Materials 4.93 5.26 0.54 0.23 | Learned Materials 2.16 1.69 0.24 0.17 | Neural Materials 1.00 0.95 0.13 0.12

headline_findings.claim: NON-UNIQUENESS WARNING that lands directly on our five gamma_po coefficients: the NVIDIA authors state that the same reflection coefficient is reachable from different (sigma, eps_r) pairs, and that a calibrated value is NOT the value you would measure on the object.
quotes: the same absolute value of a reflection coefficient (17) can be obtained for different values of conductivity and permittivity

the calibration does not necessarily lead to the same values which would be obtained by directly measuring them for each object. The reason for this is that calibration also compensates for errors in the geometry and measurements as well as modelling errors in the RT process.
headline_findings.why_it_matters_for_us: Our gamma_po values (carbon 0.90, plastic 0.28, prop 0.25, pcb 0.80, camera 0.85) are exactly this kind of lumped effective coefficient. This citation both licenses the lumping and forbids us from calling them measured material constants.

headline_findings.claim: MEASURED-vs-LITERATURE SPREAD FOR A PLASTIC, usable as an honest error bar on our own plastic eps_r 2.7. A 28 GHz bistatic campaign fitting an in-situ plexiglass panel landed at eps_r = 4.0, while the cited laboratory PMMA measurements give 2.60-2.62 over 9.5-75 GHz and ~2.6 in a wideband survey.
headline_findings.quote: For plexiglass, the estimated eps_r = 4.0 exceeds the 2.60 to 2.62 reported for PMMA in the 9.5-75 GHz range in [42] and the ~2.6 reported in [40]. We attribute this increased value to the particular sample used in our campaign, which is likely denser than typical PMMA and thus behaves as a stronger reflector.
citations_it_carries: [42] B. L. Givot, A. P. Gregory, B. Salski, F. Zentis, N. Pettit, T. Karpisz, and P. Kopyt, 'A comparison of measurements of the permittivity and loss angle of polymers in the frequency range 10 GHz to 90 GHz', EuCAP 2021
[40] S. S. Zhekov, O. Franek, G. F. Pedersen, 'Dielectric properties of common building materials for ultrawideband propagation studies', IEEE AP Magazine 62(1):72-81, 2020
headline_findings.action_for_us: Our annotation '문헌값 2.6-3.0' for plastic eps_r 2.7 can now be given a real citation ([42] Givot 2021, [40] Zhekov 2020) instead of a bare range, AND the in-situ vs bulk spread (2.6 -> 4.0, a factor 1.5) becomes our honest uncertainty statement.

headline_findings.claim: THREE DIFFERENT FLOORS, and the corpus never puts them in one place. (a) target-level electrical size kr >~ 30 (Sagitta). (b) facet edge length E > 1.5*lambda plus curvature metric E^2/(R*lambda) in 0.6-0.9 (Ziganshin journal). (c) incident ray-grid spacing delta_s <= lambda/5 i.e. 5 samples per wavelength (Sagitta). Our project currently states only a kr-vs-Mie ladder, i.e. only (a), and at a looser tolerance.

Where a measurement-grade target signature DOES enter a Sionna pipeline, it always enters by INJECTION from outside the tracer, never from the tracer. Two instances: LAMBDA injects CADFEKO UAV RCS; Temporal-GNN injects a statistical vehicular RCS model fitted to measurements. Neither computes a target signature inside Sionna.

P7_validity_floor_rows.rank: THE ONLY QUANTITATIVE FLOOR IN THE SIONNA CORPUS
P7_validity_floor_rows.rule_type: facet edge length + curvature-normalised discretisation metric

rules.meaning: facet characteristic edge length must be at least ~1.5 wavelengths to satisfy UTD assumptions
rules.q: In addition to the curvature-related metric, the facet size should be of several wavelengths in order to satisfy the UTD assumptions, typically E > 1.5 lambda.

rules.meaning: practical compromise band when one mesh must serve both backscattering and shadow prediction
rules.q: when a single mesh simultaneously has to be used for both backscattering and shadow region prediction, the interval E^2/(R*lambda) ~= 0.6-0.9 provides a practical compromise between accuracy in both regions and computational complexity

rules.rule: E^2/(R*lambda) ~ 0.5 is the point of diminishing returns for backscatter
rules.q: in the backscattering region, accuracy generally improves as the discretization becomes finer. However, the improvement becomes progressively smaller once E^2/(R*lambda) approaches approximately 0.5.

derivation_verbatim.q: Approximating a curved surface with facets introduces geometric deviation. From an electromagnetic perspective, this geometric deviation produces a phase error delta_phi ~ 2*pi*s/lambda, which should remain a small fraction of 2*pi to maintain a reasonable accuracy. ... the deviation scales as s ~ E^2/R. This leads to the parameter E^2/(R*lambda)

how_it_was_established.q: the practical operating range needs to be established empirically through comparison against analytical and full-wave reference solutions

applied_to_a_real_target.q: The parameter E^2/(R*lambda) at 3 GHz is estimated as around 0.4-0.6.

P7_validity_floor_rows.usable_by_us: YES, DIRECTLY. E^2/(R*lambda) is computable from any of our drone meshes without re-running physics. It is the single most actionable P7 result found.
P7_validity_floor_rows.caveat: It is a UTD/diffraction-driven rule for a ray+UTD pipeline. Our kernel is SBR+PO with no edge term, so the rule constrains our GEOMETRY discretisation but does not by itself validate our PO integral.

verbatim.q: to apply conventional ray tracing techniques in combination with the Uniform Theory of Diffraction (UTD) under the assumption that facets are larger than the wavelength

The approach can yield realistic results even when facets are comparable to, or smaller than, the wavelength, as edge plus vertex UTD diffraction should still complement reflection in a consistent way to yield smooth, albeit approximate, field results.
The naming convention is based on the assumption that the standard facet size for RT is several wavelengths. Hence, a facet size of 1.0 lambda is considered smaller than the standard.
The criteria for under- and over-discretizations are not strict and are chosen freely

In EM solvers such as MLFMM, facets are usually subdivided into much smaller facets, often several times smaller than the wavelength [16]. However, such a level of discretization is not necessary for ray-based simulations. The question of how finely curved surface regions need to be discretized in ray-based modeling to achieve results that match ground-truth data for smooth surfaces, remains unresolved and requires further investigation.
even when dealing with electrically small facets and edges; however, how small the facets should be is still an open question

verbatim.q: Classical scattering theory indicates that the frequency dependence of the clutter is closely tied to the scatterer's electrical size across the signal bandwidth. A practical engineering measure for this purpose is the bandwidth-induced electrical size change [55] delta(ka) = 2*pi*D_dom*B/c0 where D_dom is the size of the scattering object. When delta(ka) << 1, the clutter RCS and array responses can be approximated as frequency-flat, simplifying full-band covariance estimation. Conversely, when delta(ka) >~ O(1), the frequency-dependent scattering characteristics necessitate subband-based ...

P7_validity_floor_rows.citation: [55] E. F. Knott, J. F. Schaeffer, M. T. Tuley, Radar Cross Section, 2nd ed., Artech House, 1993
P7_validity_floor_rows.why_it_matters_for_us: This is the corpus's only formal handle on RCS-versus-bandwidth, and it belongs to our P4 band-slope problem as much as to P7. For our chamber geometry it gives a cheap, citable test of whether a per-band constant sigma is defensible.

rules.q: Electrical size is here defined as kr = 2*pi*r/lambda, where r is the sphere radius. At kr = 1, Mie resonances dominate and ray tracing methods fail, as wave effects cannot be neglected in this regime. Ray-based approximations become valid as frequency increases, with good agreement typically expected for kr >~ 30. Our simulation results (Fig. 4) demonstrate excellent agreement with Mie theory beginning at an electrical size around kr ~= 30.

rules.rule: optical region 30 <= kr <= 8000, agreement std dev ~2.5%
rules.q: the optical region where the method accurately approximates scattering with a standard deviation of ~2.5%. At higher frequencies, a low ray density region fails to resolve the wavelength, leading to an aliasing instability. The labels kr = 30 and kr = 8000 denote the boundary of the optical region and the onset of the aliasing instability, respectively.

we enforce a conservative sampling rule delta_s <= lambda/5. This converts accuracy requirements into a resolution requirement on the incident ray grid and provides a simple knob for numerical stability across frequency sweeps. This criterion implies that at least five samples per wavelength are required to accurately capture the rapidly oscillating phase terms.

rules.rule: D >> lambda as the entry condition for asymptotic methods
rules.q: Backscattering analysis for electrically large PEC objects (D >> lambda) necessitates asymptotic methods, as full-wave discretizations become computationally prohibitive.
The method is primarily intended for the GHz regime where objects are electrically large (kr <~ 10^5).

P7_validity_floor_rows.validated_against: analytical Mie for a PEC sphere; A380 aircraft at 10 GHz with a 30,000 x 30,000 ray grid over a 90 x 90 m aperture, 100 reflections max

material_choice_they_made.q: The aircraft is modeled as a PEC object, a standard approximation for metallic structures in microwave regime.

confrontation_with_our_numbers.ours: PO vs exact Mie within 1 dB from kr >= 9.06; airframes span kr 8.4 to 80; mini5pro at LTE = 8.4 and it is a measurement platform
confrontation_with_our_numbers.theirs: good agreement from kr ~= 30, at a ~2.5% std-dev standard
confrontation_with_our_numbers.honest_reading: Not a contradiction - different tolerances. 1 dB is ~26% in linear power, ten times looser than 2.5%. But our published-literature backing for operating between kr 9 and 30 is currently ZERO, and the only paper that measured the boundary put it at 30.
confrontation_with_our_numbers.required_action: Either (a) restate our floor at the tolerance we actually need for detection work and say so explicitly, or (b) mark every kr < 30 configuration as outside the published optical region. Do not keep quoting 9.06 as if it were the field's number.

P7_validity_floor_rows.paper: Zhang et al., A Unified RCS Modeling of Typical Targets for 3GPP ISAC Channel Standardization (arXiv:2505.20673, DJI M350 measurements) - RCS_ANCHOR F10, secondary corpus
P7_validity_floor_rows.rule_type: QUALITATIVE regime statement plus a facet far-field condition

verbatim.q: RCS is typically categorized into three regions-optical, Rayleigh, and resonant-based on the dimensionless size parameter ka = 2*pi*a/lambda, where a represents the characteristic size of the target and lambda is the wavelength. At GHz-level frequencies, most practical targets fall into the optical region ka >> 1, where the target size is much larger than the wavelength.

large targets are typically decomposed into smaller facets, each of which is located in the far-field region of both the transmitter and receiver. Under the assumption that there are no mutual interactions between these facets, the total RCS can be determined as the vector sum of the contributions of the individual facets

High-frequency methods such as physical optics (PO), geometric optics (GO), and the physical theory of diffraction (PTD) provide approximate solutions with reduced computational complexity but sacrifice accuracy and require corrections for specific scenarios.

P7_validity_floor_rows.verdict: States the regime taxonomy and asserts 'most practical targets fall into the optical region ka >> 1' WITHOUT a number and WITHOUT checking it for the DJI M350 they measured. A qualitative floor only.
P7_validity_floor_rows.for_us: This is the paper our absolute-sigma anchoring leans on. Its own validity statement is qualitative, so it cannot be cited as support for operating at kr 8.4.

P2_who_sourced_a_target_material_from_a_.scope: 140-paper Sionna corpus; 9 papers that put any electromagnetic property on a target were identified and all 9 were opened

'Deterministic Modeling of Dynamic ISAC' - S values cited to a WCNC 2025 building-surface measurement, target vehicle unstated

P2_who_sourced_a_target_material_from_a_.consequence_for_us: Our unresolved P2 is not a local failure. It is the state of the field, and it is stated as future work by the one group that pushed hardest. We should write it that way, with H2 as the citation, rather than apologising for it.

P7_who_stated_a_validity_floor.answer: Inside the Sionna corpus: ONE group, two documents, and the rule is about FACET SIZE (E > 1.5*lambda; E^2/(R*lambda) in 0.6-0.9), not about target electrical size. The same group says in print that the floor 'remains unresolved'.
P7_who_stated_a_validity_floor.the_number_we_actually_need: kr >~ 30 for the optical region, from SagittaSBR (arXiv:2604.09243, p8), validated against analytical Mie for a PEC sphere with ~2.5% std dev. This is in the secondary corpus and it is stricter than our own kr >= 9.06 claim.
P7_who_stated_a_validity_floor.supporting_but_qualitative: Zhang DJI M350 (arXiv:2505.20673, p4): three-region taxonomy, 'most practical targets fall into the optical region ka >> 1', no number, not checked for the M350.
P7_who_stated_a_validity_floor.consequence_for_us: We now have three citable, mutually independent floors (target kr, facet edge, ray-grid spacing) and can state all three for our meshes. But the honest headline is that mini5pro-at-LTE (kr 8.4) is below every published floor found, and we must say so instead of resting on our own sphere ladder.
